core.title: Write each user/system flow sequence step with step, intent, from, to and one artifact
core.given: A user/system flow sequence (ordered workflow steps) exists or is being written, whether you are authoring, editing, inspecting or validating it.
core.when: You author, edit, inspect or validate that user/system flow, including an unchanged sequence.
core.then: Make sure every element of the sequence is a step that transfers exactly one artifact and declares all required fields: step, intent, from, to, artifact.
prefer: Write the sequence as a flat ordered list of step elements, one artifact handoff per step (from one participant to another).
Fill all five step fields explicitly: step, intent, from, to, artifact.
avoid: Loop elements (name, condition, steps): documented but FORBIDDEN by the linearity rule (planner.user-system-flow.linearity).
Route elements (name, branches): documented but FORBIDDEN by the linearity rule (planner.user-system-flow.linearity).
A step missing any of step, intent, from, to, artifact, or a step transferring more than one artifact.
core.why: A sequence is ordered workflow steps; each step transfers one artifact between participants, so the user/system flow stays a single linear journey whose artifact flow can be checked.
evidence: Every element in the user/system flow's sequence (changed or not) is a step with non-empty step, intent, from, to and artifact fields.
No loop or route element appears in the sequence.
verification: The check inspects every user/system flow in scope and every element of its sequence: each element must be a step with non-empty step, intent, from, to and artifact fields, transferring exactly one artifact.

Loop elements (recognized by fields name, condition, steps) and route elements (recognized by fields name, branches) do not satisfy the step shape; their prohibition is owned and enforced by the linearity rule (planner.user-system-flow.linearity), and this rule's check defers that finding to it.
The check covers the whole sequence of every user/system flow in scope, not only elements touched in the diff.

fires: Planner writes a new user/system flow and lists its ordered workflow steps in the sequence.
Planner adds, reorders or edits a step in an existing user/system flow's sequence.
Planner adds a loop or route element to a user/system flow sequence.
Planner edits only user/system flow metadata (e.g. its description), and the existing unchanged sequence has to be checked against the invariant.
Planner or verifier inspects or validates an existing user/system flow whose sequence was not changed in this task.
doesNotFire: Planner edits source files, a non-user/system-flow plan artifact or an acceptance artifact, and no user/system flow or user/system flow sequence is involved.
Planner edits documentation that mentions user/system flows but contains no user/system flow sequence definition.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds of the stack, so the core's 'user/system flow' file kind and the check's 'every user/system flow in scope' can be resolved to actual files: the user/system flow spec is one of the kinds that play the plan-artifact role.

bunOnly.text: Term sequence_element (label 'Sequence elements'): element -> required fields. step: [step, intent, from, to, artifact]; loop: FORBIDDEN by linearity (name, condition, steps); route: FORBIDDEN by linearity (name, branches).
bunOnly.reason: The term id 'sequence_element' and its label are this rule's checker/finding identifiers in the ATDD-Bun realization; the element-to-required-fields mapping itself is kept generically in core:verification.

bunOnly.text: Normative text: 'step required fields: step, intent, from, to, artifact. loop (name, condition, steps) and route (name, branches) are described here but FORBIDDEN by planner.user-system-flow.linearity.'
bunOnly.reason: A verbatim quote of the legacy source's normative text carried in the Bun sidecar for traceability; the neutral core states the same obligation directly in then/avoid/verification instead of quoting.

neutralityNotes: The rule concerns the train plan artifact, so almost all of bun.json is already stack-neutral; the core keeps the text essentially verbatim. The field names step/intent/from/to/artifact and the terms train/sequence/loop/route belong to the ATDD plan-artifact schema, not to any runtime stack, so they are treated as neutral. Stack-specific residue: (1) recognizing train spec files (which the activation file_kind 'train' and the check's 'every train in scope' rely on) is delegated to the profile via roles.plan_artifact.kinds; (2) the checker term id/label and the verbatim legacy normative-text quote are realization traceability details, kept bunOnly; (3) doesNotFire's 'wagon, WMBT or acceptance file' wording was neutralized to role level ('source files, a non-train plan artifact or an acceptance artifact') without changing scope; (4) the cross-rule id planner.train.linearity is a ruleset-level reference and was kept, since the core rule set shares one id space. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so core:verification adds none.
